headline: Bitcoin slips as $35M in protocol hacks rattle sentiment and Clarity Act odds fall to 38%
summary: A rough 24 hours for crypto security: Bitcoin and Ethereum-linked protocols lost $35 million to multiple attacks, and a separate $24 million exploit drained an Arbitrum-based trading platform. Bitcoin fell 0.8% to $65,599 against that backdrop, while the Fear & Greed index sits at 31 — firmly in fear territory. The bigger macro story is the Clarity Act, the proposed US crypto regulatory framework, whose passage odds have slipped to 38% as rising oil prices and interest rates weigh on risk appetite.

winners.name: World Liberty Financial
winners.catalyst: Mirae Group's acquisition of Korbit, South Korea's oldest crypto exchange, lifted sentiment around institutional crypto adoption — and World Liberty Financial caught a bid in the resulting enthusiasm.

losers.name: Rain
losers.catalyst: Multiple attacks on Bitcoin and Ethereum-linked protocols within hours of each other soured sentiment broadly, and Rain bore the brunt of the selloff among smaller assets.

whyItMoved:
The day's story is security, not price. Multiple attacks on Bitcoin and Ethereum-linked protocols drained roughly $35 million in a matter of hours — a reminder that DeFi (decentralized finance, meaning financial applications built on public blockchains) remains a target-rich environment. A separate exploit on AFX Trade, an Arbitrum-based platform, added another $24 million to the day's losses after attackers compromised the bridge keys that control fund transfers between networks. Together, these incidents pushed sentiment firmly into fear territory, with the Fear & Greed index reading 31 out of 100.

Bitcoin's 0.8% decline to $65,599 also reflects a deteriorating macro backdrop. Oil prices and interest rates both rose on the day, reducing appetite for risk assets broadly — crypto included. The Clarity Act, the proposed US framework for regulating digital assets, saw its passage odds fall to 38% according to prediction markets, removing a potential near-term catalyst that some traders had been pricing in.

XRP barely moved (+0.10%), though the underlying dynamic is worth noting: large holders accumulated while smaller retail participants sold — a pattern that sometimes precedes sharper moves in either direction, though no clear directional signal emerged today. The one bright spot was World Liberty Financial, which jumped 9.3% after Mirae Group — a South Korean financial giant managing roughly $1 trillion in assets — acquired Korbit, South Korea's oldest crypto exchange, signaling that institutional appetite for the sector remains intact even on a difficult day.
worthKnowing: Mirae Group, one of South Korea's largest financial conglomerates with about $1 trillion in assets under management, acquired Korbit — South Korea's oldest crypto exchange — marking one of the most significant institutional entries into the country's crypto market.

AFX Trade, an Arbitrum-based trading platform, lost $24 million after attackers compromised the bridge keys controlling its cross-chain fund transfers — a distinct incident from the broader $35 million in protocol attacks reported the same day.

XRP whale wallets accumulated the token while smaller holders sold, according to on-chain data — a divergence in holder behavior that analysts typically flag as a shift in market structure, though the price barely moved on the day.
